docs.text: A new IAGLR survey shows how federal actions are disrupting Great Lakes science—lost data, careers, & collaboration. On #WorldLakeDay, we’re reminded that protecting freshwater means supporting both the science & the people behind it. 📖 #GreatLakes #FreshwaterScience
Will Great Lakes Programs Survive Major Cuts ? Our answer: The Great Lakes economy will not survive without healthy waters. Yesterday's interview with .bsky.social is now publicly available online 👇

IAGLR Executive Director Jérôme Marty joined partners in Washington, D.C. for #GreatLakesDay to highlight the importance of Great Lakes science in informing policies that protect the world’s largest freshwater system.

"It has taken over a century of bipartisan cooperation, investment and science to bring the Great Lakes back from the brink of ecological collapse ... [T]hese reckless cuts could undo the progress in just a few short years, endangering the largest surface freshwater system in the world."

Full stop, if the US abandons this type of important funding we should just find ways to pick up the tab and share any of the research or resources from our side with the Great Lakes states that need it. We've always worked historically well with them on this, no reason it can't continue.

We're a nonpartisan nonprofit working across the region to protect our most precious resource: the fresh, clean, and natural waters of the Great Lakes. Follow for updates about the lakes and how you can protect them.
